exercises.prompt: What does *Fuimos a Cancún en julio* mean?
hints: *Fuimos* can be the preterite of *ser* or of *ir*.
What follows the verb? A place introduced by *a*.

options.label: We went to Cancún in July.
options.feedback: Yes: *a* + a place shows that *fuimos* is from *ir*.

options.label: We were in Cancún in July.
options.feedback: Not yet — "we were (located) in" would be *Estuvimos en Cancún*. With *a* + place, *fuimos* is *ir*.

options.label: We are going to Cancún in July.
options.feedback: Not yet — that would be the present, *Vamos a Cancún*. *Fuimos* is past.

options.label: They went to Cancún in July.
options.feedback: Not yet — "they went" is *fueron*. The *-mos* ending means "we".

exercises.solution: **We went to Cancún in July.** *Ser* and *ir* share the preterite forms *fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron*. Here *a Cancún* shows movement towards a place, so it is *ir*. Compare *La fiesta fue genial* (The party was great: *ser*).

exercises.prompt: Put **tener** in the preterite: *Ayer ___ (yo) un examen de español.*
hints: The *yo* ending of strong preterites is *-e*, with no accent.

feedback.message: A natural guess, but *tener* has a strong preterite: stem *tuv-* + *-e*: *tuve*.
Almost — strong preterites are stressed on the stem and have no accent: *tuve*.

exercises.solution: **tuve**: *Ayer tuve un examen de español.* *Tener* → stem *tuv-* + the strong endings *-e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron*: *tuve, tuviste, tuvo…*

exercises.prompt: Put **hacer** in the preterite: *¿Qué ___ Ana el sábado?*
hints: The preterite stem of *hacer* is *hic-*; *Ana* = she.
The *él/ella* ending is *-o*, and *c* before *o* would sound like *k*.

feedback.message: Almost — *hico* would sound like "EE-ko". To keep the sound, write *z*: *hizo*.
A natural guess, but *hacer* has a strong preterite: *hizo*.
Almost — strong preterites have no accent: *hizo*.

exercises.solution: **hizo**: *¿Qué hizo Ana el sábado?* Stem *hic-* + *-o*; the *c* becomes *z* to keep its sound before *o*. The other forms keep the *c*: *hice, hiciste, hicimos, hicisteis, hicieron*.

exercises.prompt: Put **estar** in the preterite: *El verano pasado ___ (nosotros) dos semanas en Chile.*

feedback.message: Almost — *estamos* is the present. For last summer, use the preterite: *estuvimos*.
That's a different past tense (lesson 9). For a completed two-week stay, use the preterite: *estuvimos*.

exercises.solution: **estuvimos**: *El verano pasado estuvimos dos semanas en Chile.* *Estar* → *estuv-* + *-imos*. The preterite fits because the stay is a completed, bounded period (two weeks).

exercises.prompt: Put **decir** in the preterite: *En la recepción ___ que el desayuno es a las siete.* (They said…)

feedback.message: Almost — after the *j* of the stem, the ending is *-eron*: *dijeron*.
Almost — *decir* has a strong stem in the preterite: *dij-*. *Dijeron*.

exercises.solution: **dijeron**: *En la recepción dijeron que el desayuno es a las siete.* *Decir* → *dij-* + *-eron* (not *-ieron*, because the stem ends in *j*).

exercises.prompt: Put **venir** in the preterite: *¿Por qué no ___ (tú) a la fiesta?*
hints: The *tú* ending of strong preterites is *-iste*.

feedback.message: Almost — the stem changes to *vin-*: *viniste*.
Almost — the standard *tú* preterite has no final -s: *viniste*.

exercises.solution: **viniste**: *¿Por qué no viniste a la fiesta?* *Venir* → *vin-* + *-iste*. The full set: *vine, viniste, vino, vinimos, vinisteis, vinieron*.

exercises.prompt: Put **poner** in the preterite: *___ (yo) el pasaporte en la maleta.*

feedback.message: A natural guess, but *poner* has a strong preterite: *puse*.
Almost — no accent on strong preterites: *puse*.

exercises.solution: **Puse** el pasaporte en la maleta. *Poner* → *pus-* + *-e*. Full set: *puse, pusiste, puso, pusimos, pusisteis, pusieron*.

exercises.prompt: Translate: **Last year I went to Mexico.**
hints: *Ir* in the preterite, *yo* form: *fui*, followed by *a* + place.
answers: El año pasado fui a México
El año pasado yo fui a México
Fui a México el año pasado
Yo fui a México el año pasado

feedback.match: El año pasado fuí a México
feedback.message: Almost — *fui* is one syllable and has no accent.

feedback.match: El año pasado iba a México
feedback.message: That's a different past tense (lesson 9) and would suggest a habit. For one trip, use the preterite: *fui*.

feedback.match: El año pasado fui en México
feedback.message: Almost — with *ir*, the destination takes *a*: *fui a México*.

exercises.solution: **El año pasado fui a México** (or *Fui a México el año pasado*). *Fui* is the *yo* preterite of *ir* (and of *ser*), with no accent. Movement towards a place takes *a*.

exercises.prompt: Answer with a pronoun: *¿Tienes los billetes?* — *Sí, ___ tengo.*
hints: The pronoun matches the noun it replaces.

feedback.message: Almost — *billetes* is plural, so the pronoun is *los*.
Almost — *les* is an indirect object pronoun (lesson 10). For a direct object like *los billetes*, use *los*.

exercises.solution: **los**: *Sí, los tengo.* The direct object pronoun agrees with the noun it replaces: *los billetes* (masculine plural) → *los*. It goes right before the conjugated verb.

exercises.prompt: Answer with a pronoun: *¿Viste a Laura?* — *Sí, ___ vi ayer.*
hints: Direct object pronouns replace people too.

feedback.message: Not quite — for a woman as direct object, the standard pronoun is *la*: *la vi ayer*.
Almost — Laura is a woman, so *la*.
That repeats the name; the question asks for a pronoun: *la*.

exercises.solution: **la**: *Sí, la vi ayer.* *A Laura* is the direct object (with the personal *a*); the pronoun replacing it is *la*, feminine singular, placed before the verb.

exercises.prompt: *¿El billete de tren?* Which sentences correctly say **I want to buy it**? Choose all that apply.
hints: With a conjugated verb + infinitive, the pronoun can go before the conjugated verb or attached to the infinitive.

options.label: Quiero comprarlo.
options.feedback: Yes: the pronoun is attached to the infinitive.

options.label: Lo quiero comprar.
options.feedback: Yes: the pronoun goes before the conjugated verb. Just as correct.

options.label: Quiero lo comprar.
options.feedback: Not yet — the pronoun can't sit between the two verbs. Put it before *quiero* or attach it to *comprar*.

options.label: Quiero comprar lo.
options.feedback: Not yet — when it goes after an infinitive, the pronoun is written as one word with it: *comprarlo*.

exercises.solution: **Quiero comprarlo** and **Lo quiero comprar** are both correct. With a conjugated verb plus an infinitive, the object pronoun either goes before the conjugated verb or is attached to the end of the infinitive, written as one word.

exercises.prompt: Put **dar** in the preterite: *Por la tarde los turistas ___ una vuelta por el centro.*
hints: *Dar* takes the -er/-ir preterite endings, even though it's an -ar verb.

feedback.message: A natural guess for an -ar verb, but *dar* uses the -er/-ir endings: *dieron*.
Almost — *dio* is singular. *Los turistas* is plural: *dieron*.

exercises.solution: **dieron**: *Por la tarde los turistas dieron una vuelta por el centro* (went for a walk around the centre). *Dar* is irregular because it uses -er/-ir endings: *di, diste, dio, dimos, disteis, dieron*, with no accents.
